description: Each state's matched count is divided by the total number of `player_college` records, whether or not they match a college.

a.request: Match each `player_college` record to `college` on exactly equal `college_id`, and leave out records whose college isn't found. For each college `state` (a blank or missing state is its own group), give the state, its number of matched records, and that number divided by the total number of `player_college` records, counting every record, including those whose college isn't found. Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN c.state IS NULL OR TRIM(c.state) = '' THEN '' ELSE c.state END AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS fraction_of_all_records FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY CASE WHEN c.state IS NULL OR TRIM(c.state) = '' THEN '' ELSE c.state END;

b.request: For each state (blank or missing state as its own group), count the `player_college` records whose `college_id` exactly matches a `college` row in that state, and divide by the total row count of `player_college`, matched or not, without rounding
b.sql: SELECT m.state_key AS state, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS ratio FROM player_college pc JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT college_id, COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(state), ''), '') AS state_key FROM college) m ON pc.college_id = m.college_id GROUP BY m.state_key

c.request: Counting `player_college` records under the `state` of their college (matching on exactly equal `college_id`; records whose college isn't found don't count toward any state; a blank or missing state is its own group), how many records does each state have, and what share of the player-college records is that? Don't round. Each state's matched count is divided by the total number of `player_college` records, whether or not they match a college.
c.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN c.state IS NULL OR TRIM(c.state) = '' THEN NULL ELSE c.state END AS state, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS share FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON c.college_id = pc.college_id GROUP BY 1

d.request: Counting `player_college` records by the `state` of their matching college (matched on exactly equal `college_id`; records whose college isn't found are excluded from every state; a blank or missing state is its own group), how many records does each state have, and what share of all `player_college` records does each state's count represent, with the denominator including records that don't match a college? Don't round.
d.sql: SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(c.state), ''), '') AS state, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS share FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON c.college_id = pc.college_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(c.state), ''), '');
